claims.text: The initial material is an arc-melted, polished, nominally equiatomic AlCrCoFeNi alloy in the as-cast state.
The initial alloy contains approximately 79% BCC and 21% ordered B2 phases.
The initial alloy has a spinodally decomposed microstructure.
The initial alloy contains approximately 17.26 at.% Al.
Oxidation becomes pronounced above 900 °C in this alloy.
High oxygen availability accelerates outward diffusion of Al to the alloy surface.
Outward Al diffusion in air produces an externally grown Al2O3 layer.
Secondary Cr transport or oxidation produces an inner Cr2O3-enriched layer beneath the external Al2O3.
The resulting duplex Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale remains continuous and minimizes cracking or spallation.
Growth of the protective scale depletes Al from the subsurface alloy.
Al depletion transforms the underlying BCC/B2 substrate through transient FCC and sigma phases.
The transient sigma phase diminishes at higher temperatures.
Under air exposure above 900 °C, the oxide scale will be thicker and more strongly duplex than under vacuum exposure.
Under vacuum at approximately 8.82×10^-7 atm oxygen partial pressure, slower oxidation kinetics will produce only a thin, mostly alumina scale.
Vacuum exposure will cause less subsurface Al depletion and less pronounced phase transformation than air exposure.
FCC and sigma phase transitions begin at approximately 550 °C.
The high-temperature phase constitution stabilizes by approximately 1050 °C.
The proposed comparison heats identical samples to 1100 °C at 10 °C/min, using 50 °C increments and 5-minute holds, in either ambient air or vacuum.

contradictions.description: The mechanism attributes FCC and sigma formation to Al depletion caused by pronounced oxidation above 900 °C, while the boundary states that these phase transitions begin around 550 °C. The proposed oxidation-driven cause therefore does not account for the stated lower-temperature onset.
